entries.title: Constrained Consensus-Based Optimization for Decentralized Path Planning in UAV Swarms (en français: Optimisation sous contraintes fondée sur le consensus pour la planification décentralisée de trajectoires d’essaims de drones)
entries.speaker: ASSOUMANE IDI ISMAËL
entries.abstract:
The problem of safe navigation of UAV swarms in constrained environments can be rigorously for mulated as a class of distributed constrained optimization problems with time-varying feasibility sets and coupling constraints. From a mathematical perspective, this places swarmnavigation at the intersection of multi-agent optimization, consensus dynamics, and constrained control [71, 18]. 

Consensus-based optimization has emerged as a principled approach to enforce coordination in decentralized systems, particularly when agents possess only local information and communicate over sparse or time-varying graphs [74, 70]. In swarm robotics, consensus mechanisms have been successfully used to achieve formation control, collision avoidance, and collective motion [85, 75]. 

However, most existing consensus-based navigation methods either neglect hard constraints imposed by obstacles and vehicle dynamics or rely on heuristic potential fields that lack convergence and safety 570
guarantees [53]. In dynamic and uncertain environments, these limitations become critical. 

This Directed Research addresses these challenges by developing mathematically grounded methods for decentralized UAV swarm navigation based on constrained consensus-based optimization, explicitly accounting for nonconvex constraints, environmental dynamics, and uncertainty.
entries.room: Bureau du Pr Saley Bisso (Laboratoire de Mathématiques)
